name: Outer System Authority (OSA)
summary: A distant governance-and-logistics machine that treats colonies as managed systems: quotas, compliance, and calm. Authority is distributed through committees, dashboards, and the quiet power of supply.

data.mandate: Coordinate and govern Outer System settlements through standardized policy, safety frameworks, and resource allocation.

mechanisms: Layered oversight committees with narrow, enforceable scopes.
Operational dashboards that define what counts as real.
Supply chain leverage: parts, spares, and approvals move on OSA timelines.
Procedural updates that become de facto law without requiring spectacle.
style: Rules are rarely enforced harshly; they are refined, updated, and quietly made unavoidable.
Incidents are categorized to preserve institutional calm.
Communication favors certainty, even when reality is probabilistic.

presence_on_argonaut.dynamic: Authority feels everywhere and nowhere at once: local staff manage daily life, but major decisions route through distant committees.

blind_spots: Unmeasured stress and morale as leading indicators
Local expertise that contradicts central models
Compound risk from individually justified exceptions

prompt_hooks: A committee directive narrows operating margins while insisting risk is reduced.
A parts substitution is approved 'temporarily' and becomes permanent by inertia.
A local admin tries to do the right thing and discovers the paperwork is designed to prevent exactly that.
